fake-json-generator.quickAnswer: Testing an app needs data, but real user data is private and hand-writing fixtures is slow. This tool generates realistic fake JSON on the spot: pick a template (users, products, orders, or posts), choose how many records you need, and copy or download clean, valid JSON for your tests, prototypes, or demos.
keyFacts: Mock data is fake but realistic: names, emails, prices, and statuses that look like production data.
Every record gets a unique id so you can use the output directly in lists and tables.
The generator uses a seeded random function, so each Regenerate click produces a fresh dataset.
All values are generated locally; no names or emails here belong to real people.
Output is valid JSON with 2-space indentation, ready to paste into code or a .json file.
howTo: Choose a template: User, Product, Order, or Post.
Set the record count with the slider (1 to 50 records).
Click Regenerate for a fresh random dataset.
Copy the JSON or download it as mock-data.json.
Paste it into your app, test file, or API mock.
benefits: Realistic data makes UI testing far more convincing than lorem ipsum.
Zero setup: no backend or database needed for fixtures.
Instant regeneration gives fresh datasets for repeated tests.
Copy or download in one click.
limitations: Data is random and meaningless: not suitable for analytics or training models.
Templates are fixed; custom field shapes are not supported.
Emails use the example.com domain and are not real addresses.
Maximum 50 records per generation to keep the page fast.

faqs.a: No. Names, emails, and numbers are randomly generated and any resemblance to real people is coincidence. Never treat mock data as real.

faqs.q: Can I use this data in production?
faqs.a: No. It is for testing, prototyping, and demos only. Production needs real, validated data.

faqs.q: How do I get different data each time?
faqs.a: Click Regenerate. The seed changes on every click, producing a completely fresh random dataset.
A JSON array of objects with 2-space indentation. It validates as strict JSON and parses with JSON.parse in any language.

faqs.q: Can I generate more than 50 records?
faqs.a: The tool caps at 50 records per generation for performance. Generate twice and merge the arrays if you need more.
